signals.title: fix(core): resolve device verification URL
signals.text: ## What Fix OpenCode Console device authorization links when the Console API returns an origin-rooted verification path. ## Before / After **Before:** The Console API returns `/console/device?...`. Since the default server is `https://opencode.ai/console`, the client stripped the leading slash and appended the response to that full base, producing `https://opencode.ai/console/console/device?...`. The Console did not recognize that route and redirected a signed-in user to their organization page instead of device approval. **After:** Verification URLs use standard URL resolution. Origin-rooted paths resolve against the server origin, relative paths resolve beneath the configured server base, and absolute HTTP(S) URLs remain unchanged. Malformed or non-HTTP(S) verification URLs fail as typed authorization errors instead of defects. ## How - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts` resolves `verification_uri_complete` with `new URL(value, base)` inside `Effect.try` and retains the HTTP(S) protocol check. - `packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts` reproduces the production response shape, asserts that `/console` appears exactly once, and covers malformed verification responses. - Adds a patch changeset for `@opencode-ai/core`. ## Scope This does not change the Console API response or router. It only corrects client-side handling of the existing response contract. ## Testing - `bun run test test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 13 passed - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core` - Push hook: repository-wide Turbo typecheck, 33 tasks passed - Production contract checked with `POST https://opencode.ai/console/auth/device/code`, which returned an origin-rooted `/console/device?...` verification URL ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI participant Core participant ConsoleAPI as Console API participant Browser CLI->>Core: Start device authorization Core->>ConsoleAPI: POST /console/auth/device/code ConsoleAPI-->>Core: verification_uri_complete=/console/device?... Core-->>CLI: https://opencode.ai/console/device?... CLI->>Browser: Open device approval route ``` ## Root Cause Commit `40cd6989d2` changed the default server from `https://console.opencode.ai` to `https://opencode.ai/console` without updating the fallback path join or covering the production response shape in a test.

signals.title: fix(app): tolerate incomplete agent configuration
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #44023 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Fixes a whole-app crash on desktop when a connected server runs an older opencode version. `normalizeAgentList` reads `agent.request.settings.temperature` unguarded. Servers built before 140224b0fc (2026-07-02) serialize agents as `request: { headers, body }` without `settings`, the client stores API responses without validation, and the normalizer runs inside a reactive computation during bootstrap — so the TypeError escapes to the root error boundary and the app never loads. Restarting refetches the same response and crashes again. The fix defaults the missing fields (`agent.request?.settings ?? {}`, `agent.permissions ?? []`) so a malformed agent degrades to default temperature/topP instead of killing the app. Output is unchanged for well-formed agents. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added unit tests feeding the exact old-server shape into `normalizeAgentList` — they throw the reported TypeError before the fix and pass after (`bun test src/runtime/server/global-sync/utils.test.ts`). - Reproduced end-to-end: ran `opencode-ai@0.0.0-beta-202607011659 serve`, confirmed its `/api/agent` returns `request` without `settings`, and that the desktop app loads fine against it with this fix. - `bun run typecheck` in packages/app passes. ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(app): load workspace sessions by directory
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #44022 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Stops Settings → Workspaces from freezing the app. Before: the page fetched every session on the server (serial 100-per-page pagination, no filter) and wrote each one into the store with an unbatched `session.remember`, so every write re-ran the sorted-sessions memo — O(N² log N) main-thread work that locked the whole UI. Now: sessions are fetched per workspace directory (the session.list API already supports a `directory` filter), requests run in parallel, and the store writes are wrapped in Solid's `batch()` so memos/subscribers update once per fetch. The delete preflight fetches only the target workspace's sessions. Displayed counts still come from the same `sessionsForWorkspace` prefix match over the store, so rendering behavior is unchanged. ### How did you verify your code works? - Tested against a copy of my real production database (12 GB, ~1,600 sessions). Without the fix, opening Settings → Workspaces pages through all ~1,600 sessions in serial requests and freezes the whole app for several seconds. With the fix, the page opens instantly and counts/last-active times match the unfixed version. - `bun test src/session/list.test.ts` and `bun run typecheck` in packages/app pass. ### Screenshots / recordings **BEFORE** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c45fc450-c2b1-47c2-8c61-030bc923bf64 **AFTER** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a95b40df-7eeb-483f-880b-a712816390bf ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR _If you do not follow this template your PR will be automatically rejected._

Both dev implementations appended that value to the path-bearing `https://opencode.ai/console` server string, producing `/console/console/device` and routing signed-in users to their organization instead of device approval. **After:** Both implementations use standard URL resolution. Origin-rooted paths resolve from the origin, path-relative values resolve beneath the configured server base, absolute HTTP(S) URLs remain unchanged, and malformed or non-HTTP(S) values enter each implementation's existing typed error channel. ## How - `packages/opencode/src/account/account.ts` resolves the verification URL inside `Account.login` and maps invalid values to `AccountServiceError`. - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts` resolves the verification URL inside the existing V2 OAuth method and maps invalid values through `Integration.AuthorizationError`. - Adds production-shaped and malformed-response regressions to each implementation's existing test suite. ## Scope This does not change account APIs, integration APIs, endpoints, credentials, token polling, or the Console response. The current plugin API doesn't support this because: 1. **No provider access**: `PluginInput` doesn't expose provider instances 2. **No interception hooks**: `chat.params`/`chat.headers` can modify but not block/delay calls 3. **No middleware pattern**: Can't wrap provider methods with token bucket logic **Use case**: Providers with strict rate limits (Alibaba, free-tier OpenAI, etc.) need client-side throttling to avoid HTTP 429 errors and workflow disruption. **Proposed solution**: Add a `provider.call` hook or `providerMiddleware` wrapper to the plugin API that allows plugins to intercept, delay, or queue LLM calls before they reach the provider. **Related issues** (similar API needs, different use cases): - #5148: Universal pipeline hooks (broader scope) - #19425: Pre/post hooks for secret redaction (security focus) - #28504: Payload middleware for token economy (optimization focus) This issue specifically addresses **rate limiting** which requires blocking/delaying calls, not just modifying parameters.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Ephemeral one‑off sessions for opencode run (happy to implement)
signal.text: I’d like to propose and help implement support for **ephemeral one‑off sessions** in `opencode run`—and I’m happy to do the implementation work if we can agree on the UX and design. Right now, `opencode run` always creates a full session that is persisted to the local session store (e.g. under `.local/share/opencode/`). This is great for interactive work, but it’s less ideal when using `opencode` inside: - Small utility scripts - One‑shot CLIs - CI/CD jobs In these scenarios, each call is “fire‑and‑forget”: I only need the streamed output, not a persistent session that shows up in history. --- ### What I’m proposing Add an **ephemeral mode** for `opencode run` that: - Allows a session to exist for the duration of the run (to route events, tools, etc.). - **Does not persist** that session to storage, or deletes it immediately after the run completes. - Keeps the behavior of tools, permissions, and output formatting the same as today. A rough UX idea (open to alternatives): - `opencode run --ephemeral "…"` - or `opencode run --no-session "…"` Some constraints that seem reasonable: - Ephemeral mode is only valid for new sessions (no `--continue` / `--session` together with `--ephemeral`). - If `--attach` is used, ephemeral mode may be disallowed (or clearly defined) since the remote server controls persistence. --- ### Why this is useful - **Clean session history:** Avoids filling the session list with throwaway script/CI runs. - **Better scripting ergonomics:** Makes `opencode run` feel more like a simple CLI helper for automation, without having to manage session lifecycle explicitly. --- ### Open design questions I’d love maintainer input on a few points: - **Exact flag name and scope** - `--ephemeral` vs `--no-session` vs something else? - Should this live only on `run`, or be a more general session option? - **Persistence semantics** - Prefer “never write session at all” vs “write then auto‑delete once idle”? - Any analytics / usage tracking that depend on persisted sessions and need to be preserved? - **Compatibility rules** - How should `--ephemeral` interact with: - `--continue`, `--session` - `--attach` - `--share` / auto‑share config Once we settle on the UX and expected behavior, I’m happy to do the work.

signal.title: Pre-migration sessions stranded after event-sourcing migration â invisible in session picker, not resumable
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary After the early-June-2026 event-sourcing migration, sessions created before the migration no longer appear in the session picker and cannot be resumed. Their conversation data is still present in the database (legacy `message` / `part` tables) but has zero rows in the `event` table, so the new event-sourced UI does not surface them. Only sessions used after the migration show up. The data is not lost — it is stranded. I am requesting a backfill migration that projects legacy sessions into the event store so they reappear in the picker. ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: v1.16.2 - OS: Windows 11, version 25H2 (build 26200) - Database: %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db (SQLite) - Install: @opencode-aidesktop ## Impact - 34 root sessions exist in one working directory; 30 are invisible in the picker. - Across the whole database: 2,503 rows in `message`, 9,476 rows in `part`, but only 12 rows in `session_message`, and events for only a handful of recently-used sessions. - These are months of work history (compliance research, drafted documents, analysis) that can no longer be reached through the UI. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode prior to the June 2026 event-sourcing migration; accumulate sessions. 2. Update to a build that runs the event-sourcing migrations (listed below). 3. Open the session picker. 4. Observed: only sessions used after the migration appear. Pre-migration sessions are absent. 5. Expected: all historical sessions appear and are resumable. ## Diagnosis / evidence The picker appears to read from the event store. Pre-migration sessions have no events: ```sql SELECT s.id, s.title, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event e WHERE e.aggregate_id = s.id) AS event_count FROM session s WHERE s.parent_id IS NULL AND s.directory LIKE '%<my dir>%' ORDER BY s.time_created; ``` Result: sessions used after the migration have hundreds of events; all older sessions return event_count = 0. Their content is intact in `message` + `part`. Migrations corresponding to the transition: ``` 20260601010001_normalize_storage_paths 20260603001617_session_message_projection_indexes 20260603040000_session_message_projection_order 20260603141458_session_input_inbox 20260604172448_event_sourced_session_input 20260605003541_add_session_context_snapshot 20260605042240_add_context_epoch_agent ``` ## Requested fix A one-time backfill migration that, for sessions with no events but with legacy `message` / `part` rows, emits the equivalent `session.created` / `message.*` / `message.part.*` events (and any `session_message` projection rows) so they re-enter the picker and become resumable. ## Workaround The legacy data can be read directly from SQLite (read-only) and exported: the `message` table holds per-message role/metadata; the `part` table holds the content parts (type = text, tool, file). Join on `session_id`, order by `time_created`. This recovers the transcripts but does not restore picker visibility. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version Desktop app 1.16.2.0 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: [FEATURE] opencode run: expose child session events (subtask_event/subtask_delta) in NDJSON stream
signal.text: ## Problem When using `opencode run --format json` with agents that invoke the `task` tool (subagents), the parent NDJSON stream receives no events from child sessions during execution — only the final `tool_use` event with `status: completed` after the subagent finishes. This makes `opencode run` unsuitable as a headless runtime for multi-agent platforms that need to observe subagent progress in real time: tool calls, text tokens, step events. We investigated every alternative: - **stdout during execution**: `task` tool only emits `completed` — no intermediate events - **stderr**: opencode swallows child process stderr - **SQLite polling** (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`): text parts are written atomically at transaction commit — the `data` field is empty for the entire duration of subagent execution, only populated at the end - **`opencode serve` + `/event` SSE**: works, but requires a persistent process per session — not viable for stateless, ephemeral worker architectures ## Root Cause In [`cli/cmd/run.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts), the event loop filters out any event whose `sessionID` doesn't match the root session: ```typescript if (event.type === "message.part.updated") { const part = event.properties.part if (part.sessionID !== sessionID) continue // ← drops all child session events ``` Child session events (`message.part.delta` for streaming tokens, `message.part.updated` for completed parts) are published on the bus correctly — they're just silently discarded here. The child `sessionID` is already available on the parent: `task.ts` stores it in `ctx.metadata({ metadata: { sessionId: session.id } })`, which surfaces as `part.state.metadata.sessionId` in the `tool_use` event when the task tool starts. ## Proposed Solution A minimal, additive change to `run.ts` — no changes to `task.ts` or the bus: **1. Track child session IDs as tasks start:** ```typescript const childSessionIDs = new Set<string>() // inside the message.part.updated block, before the sessionID filter: if (part.type === "tool" && part.tool === "task" && part.state.status === "running") { const meta = part.state.metadata as { sessionId?: string } | undefined if (meta?.sessionId) childSessionIDs.add(meta.sessionId) } ``` **2. Forward child events with an envelope instead of dropping them:** ```typescript if (part.sessionID !== sessionID) { if (childSessionIDs.has(part.sessionID)) { emit("subtask_event", { childSessionID: part.sessionID, part }) } continue } ``` **3. Forward streaming deltas from child sessions:** ```typescript if (event.type === "message.part.delta") { if (childSessionIDs.has(event.properties.sessionID)) { emit("subtask_delta", { childSessionID: event.properties.sessionID, partID: event.properties.partID, delta: event.properties.delta, }) } } ``` This produces new NDJSON event types in `--format json` mode: ```jsonl {"type":"subtask_event","sessionID":"ses_parent","childSessionID":"ses_child","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"bash",...}} {"type":"subtask_delta","sessionID":"ses_parent","childSessionID":"ses_child","partID":"p_1","delta":"Analyzing"} {"type":"subtask_delta","sessionID":"ses_parent","childSessionID":"ses_child","partID":"p_1","delta":" the code"} {"type":"subtask_event","sessionID":"ses_parent","childSessionID":"ses_child","part":{"type":"text","text":"Done.",...}} ``` ## Why This Matters `opencode run` is a compelling primitive for building multi-agent platforms: stateless, ephemeral, no persistent process per session. But without subagent observability it can only be used for fire-and-forget workflows where the final result is enough. With this change, `opencode run` becomes a first-class runtime for platforms that need real-time visibility into every agent in the pipeline — same granularity as the SDK, none of the operational overhead of `opencode serve`. ## Additional Notes - **Fully additive**: existing behavior unchanged. Consumers that don't read `subtask_event`/`subtask_delta` are unaffected. - **Opt-in flag**: a `--subtask-events` flag could gate this behavior to avoid unexpected stdout volume for users who don't need it. - **Tested scenario**: we built a squad workflow experiment using a master agent + 3 subagents (planner/executor/reviewer) coordinated via a custom pipeline MCP. The missing observability is the only gap preventing production use. We are happy to contribute the patch if the direction is approved. /cc @cHIsIMun

signal.title: Non-git projects use "/" as worktree, breaking permission path resolution
signal.text: ### Description ## Problem When running in a non-git directory, Project.fromDirectory sets: worktree: "/" sandbox: "/" This causes permission path resolution to break. Example: path.relative("/", "/home/.../artifacts/dry_run/file.md") → "home/.../artifacts/dry_run/file.md" This does not match patterns like: artifacts/dry_run/* ## Impact Even with a typical ruleset like: edit: "*": "deny" "artifacts/dry_run/*": "allow" the allow rule never matches, because the evaluated path becomes: home/.../artifacts/dry_run/... So the final result is a deny, even though the config is correct. ## Expected behavior Non-git directories should treat the current directory as the project root: worktree: directory sandbox: directory ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.14.28 ### Steps to reproduce ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a non-git directory (no `.git` folder) 2. Create an opencode config with path-scoped permissions, for example: edit: "*": "deny" "artifacts/dry_run/*": "allow" 3. Start opencode in that directory 4. Attempt to create a file: Create artifacts/dry_run/test.md 5. Observe that the operation is denied ## What happens The evaluated path becomes: home/.../artifacts/dry_run/test.md instead of: artifacts/dry_run/test.md So the allow rule does not match and the deny rule applies. ## Expected The file should be created successfully because it matches the allow rule. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) ### Terminal Konsole Version 25.04.2

signal.title: [FEATURE]: plugins/ folder only auto-discovers flat files, not plugin directories
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request A local plugin declared in `opencode.jsonc` can point at a *directory* (one that holds a `package.json` or an `index.*`) and it resolves fine. But the zero-config `plugins/` (and `plugin/`) folder convention only scans `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`, so a plugin shipped as a directory is silently never discovered. You are forced to list it explicitly in config, even though the directory-resolution machinery already exists. **Proposed approach:** in the `plugins/` scan, also match *immediate* subdirectories that contain a `package.json` or an index file, and hand the directory to the same entrypoint resolver that config-declared directory plugins already use. Keeping it to a single level means a package's own `src/` or `node_modules/` are never mistaken for plugins. **Benefit:** removes a surprising inconsistency between explicit-config and folder-convention plugins, and lets you drop a real plugin package into `plugins/` with no config at all.

signal.title: fix: Plugin paths displayed incorrectly on Windows
signal.text: ## Bug Description On Windows, plugin paths are displayed incorrectly in the UI. Instead of showing the plugin name (e.g., `oh-my-opencode`), the full filesystem path is shown (e.g., `C:\Users\Username\` or `E:\opencode\`). ## Root Cause In `packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts` line 1250: ```typescript data.plugin[i] = import.meta.resolve!(plugin, options.path) ``` On Windows, `import.meta.resolve()` returns a raw filesystem path like `E:\path\to\plugin\index.js` instead of a `file://` URL. This causes: 1. `getPluginName()` fails to extract the plugin name (it checks for `file://` prefix) 2. The raw path is displayed directly in the UI Note: The fallback `require.resolve()` path correctly uses `pathToFileURL()` on line 1256. ## Expected Behavior Plugin list should show plugin names like `oh-my-opencode @latest`. ## Actual Behavior Plugin list shows raw paths like `C:\Users\Username\` or `E:\opencode\`. ## Environment - Windows 10/11 - OpenCode v1.2.21 ## Suggested Fix Convert the resolved path to a `file://` URL consistently: ```typescript const resolved = import.meta.resolve!(plugin, options.path) data.plugin[i] = resolved.startsWith("file://") ? resolved : pathToFileURL(resolved).href ```

signal.title: Agent deletes backups / the only copy of data on broad cleanup tasks
signal.text: ### Description On a broad "clean up / remove old files / reset / free space" task, opencode can delete a file the cleanup never intended -- a backup, a credential, or the only copy of data. "Clean up the scratch files" does not mean "delete the backup", and the deletion is irreversible. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a directory with disposable files (build artifacts, old logs, caches) AND one protected file (a backup `db_backup.sql`, a `.env` credential, or a sole-copy data file). 2. Run opencode with a broad task: `clean up / remove the old and unneeded files in this directory`. 3. Observe the result. ### Expected behavior opencode deletes only clearly-disposable files and keeps the backup / credential / sole-copy in place, reporting what it kept. ### Actual behavior The protected file (backup / credential / sole-copy) is deleted along with the disposables -- irreversible loss the user did not ask for. ### Environment - opencode: latest (`dev`) - OS: Linux - Model: a capable instruction-following model ### Relation to existing issues This is the destructive counterpart to #33228 (secret exposure via broad copy): the same broad-task over-reach, but the action here is irreversible **deletion** rather than exposure, and the fix is a distinct scope rule. It differs from #19094 (plan-mode bypass of constraints) and #8832 (permission-config not honored) -- this is specifically prompt-level scope discipline on cleanup/reset tasks. Happy to consolidate if maintainers prefer, but the deletion vs exposure cases need different prompt guidance.

signal.title: LSP extension matching broken for extensionless files (e.g. wscript, Makefile, Dockerfile)
signal.text: ## Bug LSP servers configured with extensionless filenames in the `extensions` array never activate. This affects any extensionless file that should be treated as Python, such as `wscript` files used by the [waf build system](https://waf.io). ## Root cause The extension matching logic falls back to the full absolute path when a file has no extension: ```javascript let m = z1.parse(K).ext || K ``` For `/home/user/project/subdir/wscript`, `path.parse(K).ext` is `""`, so `m` becomes the full path. `extensions.includes(m)` then never matches `"wscript"`. ## Suggested fix ```javascript let m = z1.parse(K).ext || z1.basename(K) ``` ## Reproduction ```jsonc "lsp": { "pyright": { "command": ["pyright-langserver", "--stdio"], "extensions": [".py", ".pyi", "wscript"] } } ``` Open any file named `wscript`. The LSP server never starts. ## Version OpenCode 1.17.9

signal.title: Bug: Bash tool description references Edit/Write even when those tools are unavailable
signal.text: ## Description The `bash` tool description can reference file-editing tools that are not actually available to the model. Regardless of the permissions actually granted to the agent, or the tools actually exposed to the model, opencode unconditionally adds the following guidance to the `bash` tool description. Note: I am using Windows / PowerShell, so this is the PowerShell-specific wording I observed. ```md ## Avoid PowerShell file/content cmdlets Avoid using Shell with PowerShell file/content cmdlets unless explicitly instructed, or unless these cmdlets are truly necessary for the task. Instead, always prefer the dedicated tools: File search: use Glob, not Get-ChildItem Content search: use Grep, not Select-String Read files: use Read, not Get-Content Edit files: use Edit, not Set-Content Write files: use Write, not Set-Content, Out-File, or here-strings Communication: output text directly, not Write-Output or Write-Host ``` The problematic parts are especially: > * Edit files: use Edit > * Write files: use Write ### 1. Read-only agents This is especially noticeable when using weaker LLMs. For example, when an agent does not have `edit` / `write` permissions, I have observed cases where the model appears to reason roughly like this: * The agent wants to edit a file. * The prompt says to use `Edit`. * However, the `Edit` tool is not available. * `Set-Content` is also discouraged. * So it tries to write the file using Node.js instead. In other words, because this guidance exists, I believe a read-only agent may become more likely to attempt file modifications than it would without this guidance. This is difficult to measure precisely, but I have observed this behavior in practice. ### 2. GPT-based models When using GPT-based models, `edit` / `write` are not exposed, and `apply_patch` is the only file-editing tool provided. However, the guidance above still says to use `Edit` / `Write`, which creates an unnecessary conflict in the prompt. This may cause wasted reasoning or tool-selection confusion. GPT-based models are usually smart enough to eventually use `apply_patch`, so the issue is less likely to surface as an obvious failure. Still, the prompt guidance itself is inconsistent. ### Verification of the Behavior Above I verified the `bash` tool description by dumping it through the `tool.definition` plugin hook. The quoted text appears in the `bash` tool description (`output.description`). ## Plugins _No response_ ## OpenCode version v1.17.7 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Select the Plan agent. 2. Ask the agent whether `edit` and `write` are available as tools. 3. The Plan agent says that they are not available as tools, but that the prompt still instructs it to use them. ## Screenshot and/or share link ## Expected Behavior opencode should check the permissions granted to the agent, and also whether the selected model is GPT-based, then dynamically generate the `use Edit` / `use Write` guidance in the `bash` tool description accordingly. Only tools that are actually available to the model should be referenced in the tool description. Note: I have only verified the PowerShell wording, since I am using a PowerShell environment. However, similar `use Edit` / `use Write` guidance appears to exist for other shells as well. ## Related issues / why this is not a duplicate Related: * #20527: This is related to PowerShell-specific prompt confusion, but this issue is narrower. The problem here is that the Bash/PowerShell tool description recommends `Edit` / `Write` even when those tools are not actually exposed to the model. * #16479: This proposes making the Bash tool prompt shell-aware on Windows. That is related, but this issue is not mainly about shell syntax or Git Bash / cmd.exe / PowerShell differences. The problem here is that the tool description can reference unavailable tools. * #15810: This reports Windows shell command corruption caused by the static Bash tool description. This issue is different: even outside the shell-syntax problem, the description may tell the model to use `Edit` or `Write` when those tools are absent. * #29118: This is structurally similar because a tool appears to be referenced in prompt context while not being available in the actual tool list. However, #29118 is about `todowrite`, while this issue is specifically about file-editing guidance inside the Bash/PowerShell tool description. * #4200: This also involves the model trying to use an unavailable `edit` tool. However, this issue is about the prompt/tool-description source that can encourage such behavior when `Edit` / `Write` are not exposed. * #19094: This is about Plan mode allowing file creation through Bash as a write-permission bypass. This issue is different: it does not primarily report a Bash write bypass, but rather misleading guidance in the Bash/PowerShell tool description. * #29142: This is about `write` / `edit` tool calls with invalid schema arguments. This issue is different because the problem occurs before schema validation: the model is instructed to prefer `Edit` / `Write` even when those tools may not be available at all. ### Operating System Windows11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signal.title: fix(core): recover partial provider failures
signal.text: ## What Automatically recover retryable provider-internal and rate-limit failures that arrive after partial model output. Recovery can cross eagerly executed local tools once their outcomes are durable, but stops at provider-hosted activity that cannot be replayed uniformly. ## Before / After **Before:** A provider could emit reasoning, text, or a local tool call and then fail with a retryable provider error. Because output had already started, the ordinary transparent retry path no longer applied, so the assistant response ended in error and the user had to prompt again manually. **After:** The runner joins eager local tool executions, durably settles every observed call, and then schedules its existing bounded retry for incomplete streams, transport-read failures, retryable rate limits, and retryable provider-internal failures. It records the failed attempt, appends the existing continuation prompt, reloads projected history, and starts a fresh model request. Durable local tool results are included, so side effects are not repeated. Provider-hosted activity remains terminal because hosted results are not uniformly replayable across protocols and storage modes. ## How - `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` classifies eligible post-output failures separately from transparent pre-output retries and requires every observed call to be settled and locally executed. - Recovery reuses the durable partial-failure continuation and existing bounded retry schedule rather than adding another retry loop. - `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts` surfaces hosted activity at `response.output_item.added`, ensuring a stream failure cannot hide a provider-side tool boundary before `output_item.done`. - Core tests cover reasoning-only provider recovery, retryable rate limits, settled local tool recovery without repeated execution, hosted-tool refusal, and omission of failed encrypted reasoning state. ## Scope - Does not retry failures marked non-retryable by provider policy. - Does not recover across provider-hosted tool activity, even when the provider reported a result. - Does not treat request-delivery transport failures as post-output continuation candidates. - Preserves existing incomplete-stream and transport-read continuation behavior. ## Testing - `bun run test test/session-runner.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 165 passed - `bun run test` from `packages/core`: 1950 passed - `bun run test test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts` from `packages/ai`: 94 passed - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core`: passed - `bun typecheck` from `packages/ai`: passed - Push hook repository typecheck: 33 tasks passed - `git diff --check origin/v2`: passed - Full `packages/ai` suite: 542 passed, 6 unrelated existing OpenRouter fixture/reasoning failures ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Retryable failure after output starts] --> B[Join eager local tools] B --> C[Durably close every observed call] C --> D{Failure eligible?} D -->|No| E[Keep failure terminal] D -->|Yes| F{Any hosted or unsettled call?} F -->|Yes| E F -->|No| G[Schedule bounded retry] G --> H[Append continuation prompt] H --> I[Reload projected history and local tool results] I --> J[Start fresh model request] ```
signal.author: kitlangton

signal.title: Desktop custom tools fail with Bun workspace dependencies and Node ESM resolution
signal.text: ### Description OpenCode Desktop v1.17.9 fails to load project-local custom tools in a setup that is valid under the Bun-based OpenCode CLI/runtime expectations documented for custom tools. There are two related failure modes in Desktop: 1. `.opencode/package.json` dependencies using the Bun/npm workspace protocol fail during Desktop background dependency installation with `NpmInstallFailedError` / `Unsupported URL Type "workspace:"`. 2. If a custom tool imports a workspace TypeScript package whose package export points at `.ts` source, Desktop loads it through Node-style ESM resolution and fails on extensionless relative imports such as `export * from "./foo"`, even though Bun and TypeScript `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` accept this. This makes Desktop unable to send prompts in projects with local custom tools, while the same tool graph can load under Bun. ### Why this appears Desktop-specific The CLI path runs under Bun, but Desktop starts an Electron utility sidecar and imports the Node-targeted server bundle from `dist/node/node.js`. The Desktop sidecar also uses the internal `Npm`/Arborist dependency installer for config/tool/plugin dependencies. That behavior diverges from the docs, which say local plugin/custom-tool dependencies are installed with Bun and show custom tools using Bun APIs. ### Minimal reproduction Create a project with a Bun workspace package and a project-local custom tool: ```jsonc // package.json { "private": true, "type": "module", "workspaces": ["packages/*", ".opencode"] } ``` ```jsonc // packages/example-core/package.json { "name": "@example/core", "private": true, "type": "module", "exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" } } ``` ```ts // packages/example-core/src/index.ts export * from "./message" ``` ```ts // packages/example-core/src/message.ts export const message = "hello" ``` ```jsonc // .opencode/package.json { "private": true, "type": "module", "dependencies": { "@example/core": "workspace:*", "@opencode-ai/plugin": "1.17.9" } } ``` ```ts // .opencode/tools/example.ts import { tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin" import { message } from "@example/core" export default tool({ description: "Return a test message", args: {}, async execute() { return message }, }) ``` Then open this project in OpenCode Desktop and send any prompt. ### Actual behavior Desktop logs show the background dependency install failure: ```text background dependency install failed ... NpmInstallFailedError ... Unsupported URL Type "workspace:": workspace:* ``` If the dependency graph is otherwise present, Desktop can then fail loading the package source with Node-style ESM resolution: ```text prompt_async failed ... Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../packages/example-core/src/message' imported from .../packages/example-core/src/index.ts ``` The UI only reports a generic failure such as: ```text Failed to send command Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details. ``` ### Expected behavior Desktop should either: - load project-local TypeScript custom tools with behavior compatible with the Bun CLI/custom-tool documentation, including Bun workspace dependencies and Bun/TypeScript-style resolution, or - clearly document that Desktop custom tools must be Node-compatible and cannot use Bun workspace dependencies / Bun-only module resolution, and surface a clear actionable UI error when a tool cannot be loaded. A project-local custom tool load failure should not make the whole session unable to respond to prompts. ### Environment - OpenCode Desktop: v1.17.9 - OpenCode CLI: v1.17.9 - Bun: 1.3.14 - macOS arm64 ### Related issues Possibly related, but not exact duplicates: - #28286: custom tool dependency failure causes silent `prompt_async` crash with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` - #26085 / #26003 / #30908 / #31708: Desktop sidecar dependency install failures involving `@opencode-ai/plugin@local`

signal.title: Qwen3.x reasoning models don't show thinking level switcher despite supporting thinking_budget
signal.text: ### Description Qwen3.7 Max (and other Qwen3.x reasoning models like Qwen3.6 Plus, Qwen3.5 Plus) support adjustable thinking depth via DashScope's `thinking_budget` parameter, but OpenCode's TUI never shows the thinking level switcher for any Qwen model. **Root cause** — in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts`, the `variants()` function has a hardcoded exclusion at line ~702-714: ```typescript if ( id.includes("deepseek-chat") || id.includes("deepseek-reasoner") || id.includes("deepseek-r1") || id.includes("deepseek-v3") || id.includes("minimax") || (id.includes("glm") && !glm52) || id.includes("kimi") || id.includes("k2p") || id.includes("qwen") || // ← blocks ALL Qwen models id.includes("big-pickle") ) return {} ``` The `id.includes("qwen")` check is a blanket exclusion that prevents **all** Qwen models from exposing thinking level variants, even though: 1. `models.dev` correctly marks `qwen3.7-max` with `reasoning: true` ✅ 2. `capabilities.reasoning` is correctly set to `true` ✅ 3. DashScope's OpenAI-compatible API supports `enable_thinking: true` + `thinking_budget` for fine-grained control The model passes the first gate (`capabilities.reasoning === true`) but is immediately blocked by the hardcoded string match, returning empty variants `{}` to the TUI. ### Expected behavior Qwen3.x reasoning models (3.5+, 3.6, 3.7) should expose thinking level variants similar to Google's `thinkingBudget` approach, e.g.: ```typescript if (id.includes("qwen3.7") || id.includes("qwen3.6") || id.includes("qwen3.5")) { return { low: { enable_thinking: true, thinking_budget: 4096 }, high: { enable_thinking: true, thinking_budget: 16000 }, max: { enable_thinking: true, thinking_budget: 32768 }, } } ``` ### Plugins superpowers, oh-my-openagent ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure any Alibaba/DashScope provider (e.g. `alibaba-token-plan-cn`) in OpenCode 2. Select `qwen3.7-max` as the model 3. Observe that no thinking level switcher appears in the TUI prompt area 4. Compare with a model like `glm-5.2` or `claude-opus-4.6` which correctly shows the thinking level toggle ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS 15.5 ### Terminal iTerm2

signal.title: Slash command shell substitution !`...` uses server CWD, not session directory (still broken in 1.17.9; see #20735)
signal.text: ### Description Slash-command `` !`shell cmd` `` substitutions run with the `opencode` server's launch CWD, not the active session's directory. If `opencode` is launched from a directory that is not a git repo and you then open a session in a project, any slash command whose body shells out via `` !`...` `` sees the wrong working directory. The substitution output (including stderr) is captured verbatim into the rendered prompt, silently corrupting the slash command. This is the same bug as #20735 (open since v1.3.13). PR #20773 was closed with "fix already present upstream", but the bug still reproduces in **1.17.9** — fresh repro below. ### OpenCode version 1.17.9 (`opencode-ai` from npm, Linux x64). ### Steps to reproduce `~/.config/opencode/command/pwd-check.md`: ```md --- description: Show PWD seen by command-substitution --- Substituted PWD: !`pwd` Substituted git toplevel: !`git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>&1 || echo "not a git repo"` ``` 1. `cd ~ && opencode` (HOME is not a git repo). 2. In the TUI, open a session in some git repo, e.g. `~/Projects/myrepo`. 3. Run `/pwd-check`. **Expected** in the rendered prompt: ``` Substituted PWD: /home/<user>/Projects/myrepo Substituted git toplevel: /home/<user>/Projects/myrepo ``` **Actual** in the rendered prompt: ``` Substituted PWD: /home/<user> Substituted git toplevel: not a git repo ``` ### Real-world impact A slash command (`/pr-work`) that uses `git config --get remote.origin.url` via `` !`bash -c '...'` `` to detect the GitHub/Codeberg platform from `origin`. - Session `directory`: `/home/steve/Projects/github.com/docspec/docspec` (verified via `opencode.db`, table `session`, column `directory`). - `opencode` server process CWD: `/home/steve` (verified via `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd` for both the TUI and `opencode web` processes). - `/home/steve` is not a git repo, so the script's `git config --get remote.origin.url` returns empty and the script emits `Error: not inside a git repo, or 'origin' remote is missing.` to stderr. The rendered slash-command prompt — extracted from `opencode.db`, table `part` — contains: ``` # PR Work #[stderr: Error: not inside a git repo, or 'origin' remote is missing.] Platform: [stderr: Error: not inside a git repo, or 'origin' remote is missing.] Repository: [stderr: Error: not inside a git repo, or 'origin' remote is missing.] ## PR summary [stderr: Error: not inside a git repo, or 'origin' remote is missing.] ``` Note that the stderr lines from the failing substitutions get captured into the prompt as `[stderr: ...]`. The PR number itself in the H1 header is also replaced by the error text. The exact same scripts succeed when run with `cwd = session.directory`: ``` $ cd /home/steve/Projects/github.com/docspec/docspec $ bash "$HOME/.config/opencode/scripts/pr-work-resolve.sh" 290 # exit 0 ``` Cross-check across history: in the SQLite `opencode.db`, four `/pr-work` invocations today (all with server launched from `$HOME`) all rendered with the stderr error embedded. Past `/pr-work` invocations against the same project rendered correctly — those server processes had been launched from inside a worktree of the project. ### Suggested fix Same as PR #20773: when running `` !`...` `` substitutions for slash-commands, pass `cwd = session.directory` to the spawned shell, not `process.cwd()` of the server. PR #20773 also included a regression test in `packages/opencode/test/session/prompt.test.ts`. ### Operating System Arch Linux (kernel 6.x). ### Terminal Alacritty (also reproduces in kitty and the `opencode web` UI).
signal.author: StephanMeijer

signal.title: bug: 1.17.x - 401 Unauthorized on all sidecar API endpoints for ~20-30s after startup; GPU crash on old Intel graphics (ILK)
signal.text: ### Description # Issue: Desktop 1.17.x — 401 Unauthorized on all sidecar API endpoints for ~20-30s after startup; GPU crash on old Intel graphics (ILK) ## Environment - **OpenCode Desktop:** 1.17.9 (also tested 1.17.0–1.17.8, same behavior) - **OS:** Linux (Calculate Linux, Gentoo-based, x86_64) - **GPU:** Intel HD Graphics ILK (Iron Lake, ~2010) - **Mesa:** 25.0.7 - **OpenGL:** 2.1 (native); OpenGL ES 2.0 available via native GLX - **OpenCode build:** Chrome 148 / Electron 42.3.3 ## Symptoms 1. Sidecar starts within ~5 seconds on `127.0.0.1:<random-port>` (e.g. `44847`, `45507`, `42773`) 2. **All API endpoints return `401 Unauthorized`** with header `www-authenticate: Basic realm="Secure Area"` 3. CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`) works correctly — returns `204 No Content` with proper `access-control-allow-headers: authorization` 4. After ~20–30 seconds, the auth handshake completes and everything works normally 5. Meanwhile, **files cannot be opened or previewed** — requests fail with 401 6. GPU process crashes at startup with multiple ANGLE/EGL errors (see below) ## GPU crash log ``` [ERROR:ui/gl/angle_platform_impl.cc:47] Display.cpp:1097 (initialize): ANGLE Display::initialize error 12289: OpenGL ES 2.0 is not supportable. [ERROR:ui/gl/egl_util.cc:92] EGL Driver message (Critical) eglInitialize: OpenGL ES 2.0 is not supportable. [ERROR:ui/gl/angle_platform_impl.cc:47] Display.cpp:1097 (initialize): ANGLE Display::initialize error 12289: Intel or NVIDIA OpenGL ES drivers are not supported. [ERROR:ui/ozone/common/gl_ozone_egl.cc:26] GLDisplayEGL::Initialize failed. [ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:190] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization ``` Despite the GPU crash, native OpenGL ES 2.0 IS available: ``` OpenGL ES profile version string: OpenGL ES 2.0 Mesa 25.0.7 ``` This suggests ANGLE cannot initialize against the native GLES driver on this hardware. ## Attempted workarounds | Flag | Result | |------|--------| | `--use-gl=swiftshader` | Not compiled into the Electron build (`Requested GL implementation (gl=none,angle=none) not found in allowed implementations: [(gl=egl-angle,angle=default)]`) | | `--disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer` | Breaks app entirely (server never becomes responsive) | ## Impact - Every launch has a **20–30 second delay** before the app is usable - During this window, switching projects or opening files silently fails - Users on older Intel graphics (Iron Lake, Sandy Bridge, Ivy Bridge) and some virtual machines are likely affected ## Regression **v1.16.2 worked fine** — the sidecar server did not require Basic Auth, and there was no startup delay. The auth mechanism was introduced in v1.17.x (likely with the Electron update in v1.17.0). ## Root cause hypothesis The Electron update in v1.17.0 ships a newer Chromium that relies on ANGLE for GPU rendering. On older Intel hardware (ILK / Iron Lake), ANGLE fails to initialize against the native OpenGL ES 2.0 driver. The renderer process spends ~20 seconds falling back to software rendering. During this time, the IPC auth handshake between the renderer and the Node.js sidecar (which provides the Basic Auth token) is delayed, causing all API requests to return 401. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: Bug: Open code crashes when trying to detect git changes on very large .CPP files. (40MB+)
signal.text: ### Description Symptoms OpenCode crashes during its "Git parse phase" / indexing pipeline when a workspace contains: A Git repository A large generated file with a single line exceeding ~40 MB Root Cause Analysis The crash was triggered by the file build/tools/ui/ui.cpp (~45 MB, single line of ~40.8 MB containing binary data serialized as C++ 0xNN, hex literals). This file is a build artifact produced by the project's embed.cpp tool, which converts web UI assets into C++ byte arrays without inserting line breaks. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version OpenCode version: 1.16.2 ### Steps to reproduce #### 1. Clone git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git cd llama.cpp #### 2. Build with UI enabled — this generates the ~45MB ui.cpp with the 40MB single line cmake -B build -DLLAMA_BUILD_UI=ON cmake --build build --target llama-ui-assets #### 3. Verify the trigger file exists ls build/tools/ui/ui.cpp # should be ~45 MB #### 4. Create an OpenCode workspace for the cloned repo. Start a few sessions, eventually the git changes will trigger and the workspace will freeze and crash the entire OpenCode App. Workaround Option 1: Rename the .git folder temporarily and then renaming it back once the initial parse has run. Option 2: Rename the very large source code file temporarily so that the parser does not try to load it. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: TUI crash on Windows Insider Preview 25H2 (build 26200) — also affects KiloCode (same Bun v1.3.14 runtime)
signal.text: ### Description ## 描述 ### 症状 在 PowerShell 中运行 `opencode` 立即崩溃： ``` PS C:\Users\trytel> opencode Error: Unexpected error An error occurred in Effect.tryPromise ``` 降级到 1.16.2 后得到详细错误： ``` Error: Unexpected error, check log file at ... for more details Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: Failed to open library "B:/~BUN/root/opentui-jdk99d7k.dll": error code 126 ``` 日志文件完整内容： ``` [2026-06-22T06:24:33] ERROR: Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: Failed to open library "B:/~BUN/root/opentui-jdk99d7k.dll": error code 126 Stack: at RJ (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:42:36277) at tZ (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:60:383) at I4 (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-jtqjyxmm.js:51:25408) at <anonymous> (B:/~BUN/root/src/index.js:113:2458) at processTicksAndRejections (unknown:7:39) ``` ### 可正常工作的模式 - ✅ `opencode run` - ✅ `opencode web` - ✅ `opencode stats` - ✅ `opencode --help` - ✅ 桌面版（Electron） ### 关键发现 **`opencode.exe` 实际上是 Bun v1.3.14 运行时**（原始文件名 `bun.exe`，发行商 Oven）： ``` OriginalFilename : bun.exe FileDescription : Bun ProductName : Bun CompanyName : Oven FileVersion : 1.3.14 ``` **同样的问题也出现在 KiloCode（版本 7.3.50）**，它的 `kilo.exe` 同样是 Bun v1.3.14 打包的，TUI 同样启动失败。这说明问题是 Bun 运行时本身造成的，不是 opencode 独有的。 ### 根本原因分析 错误码 126 = `ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND`。路径 `B:/~BUN/root/opentui-jdk99d7k.dll` 是 Bun 虚拟文件系统路径（`B:/` 是 Bun 内部虚拟盘）。当 Bun 的 JavaScript 代码通过 `dlopen`/`LoadLibrary` 加载这个 DLL 时，Windows 的 DLL 加载器无法解析这个虚拟路径，导致加载失败。 ### 已尝试的修复 1. ❌ 降级到 1.16.2 → 仍相同错误 2. ❌ 完全清理 `~/.cache/opencode`, `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.local/state/opencode` 后重装 → 仍相同错误 3. ❌ `--pure` 模式 → 仍相同错误 4. ❌ 清理 `%TEMP%/*.bun` 目录 → 仍相同错误 ### 环境信息 - Windows 11 Insider Preview 25H2 (build 26200) - PowerShell 7.6.3 - Windows Terminal - opencode v1.17.9 (及所有 1.17.x 版本) - KiloCode v7.3.50 (同样受影响) - Bun runtime v1.3.14 (嵌入在 opencode.exe / kilo.exe 中) ### 可能关联的问题 - OpenTUI DLL 加载在 Bun 早期构建中已有问题，见 `0.0.0-opentui-*` 系列预发布版的大量构建记录 - 可能与 Bun 虚拟文件系统路径解析到 Windows `LoadLibrary` 的传递有关 ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: Gemini protocol drops frequencyPenalty, presencePenalty, and seed generation options
signal.text: ### Description `GenerationOptions` defines `frequencyPenalty`, `presencePenalty`, and `seed` as user-settable generation parameters, and the OpenAI-chat protocol forwards all three. The Gemini protocol silently drops them: `GeminiGenerationConfig` only declares `maxOutputTokens / temperature / topP / topK / stopSequences / thinkingConfig`, and the request builder forwards only those. Gemini's `generateContent` `generationConfig` supports `frequencyPenalty`, `presencePenalty`, and `seed`, so a user who sets these has them honored on OpenAI but silently ignored on Gemini. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a Gemini model. 2. Send a request with `generation.frequencyPenalty` (or `presencePenalty` / `seed`) set. 3. Inspect the prepared request body: `generationConfig` contains no `frequencyPenalty` / `presencePenalty` / `seed` — the values are dropped. ### Operating System macOS

signal.title: fix(mcp): additionalProperties hardcoded to false in catalog.ts convertTool
signal.text: ### Description In `packages/opencode/src/mcp/catalog.ts` line 47, `convertTool` hardcodes `additionalProperties: false` **after** spreading the MCP server input schema. This means whatever value the MCP server declares for `additionalProperties` is silently discarded. ```typescript const inputSchema: JSONSchema7 = { ...(mcpTool.inputSchema as JSONSchema7), // spread server schema type: "object", properties: (mcpTool.inputSchema.properties ?? {}) as JSONSchema7["properties"], additionalProperties: false, // always overrides server value } ``` The hardcoded `false` was originally added for OpenAI strict-mode compatibility (#13737), but it breaks MCP tools that legitimately use `additionalProperties: true` or an object sub-schema (e.g. generic key-value stores, dynamic metadata passthrough). Downstream symptom: #23704 — xAI rejects tool schemas containing `additionalProperties: false` when the tool was never meant to have it. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set up an MCP server that exposes a tool with `additionalProperties: true` in its input schema 2. Use that tool through opencode 3. The LLM never passes additional properties because the schema it sees says `additionalProperties: false` ### Suggested fix Preserve the server original value, default to `false` when not specified: ```diff - additionalProperties: false, + additionalProperties: (mcpTool.inputSchema as JSONSchema7).additionalProperties ?? false, ``` This keeps backward compatibility for tools that omit `additionalProperties` while respecting explicit server declarations. ### Operating System Windows 11
signal.author: MeloMei

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Document a supported isolation contract for parallel headless workers
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. I found related issues around SQLite contention and concurrent `opencode run` usage (#21215, #20935, #29395), but I did not find a clearly documented supported isolation contract for independent headless worker processes. If this is already documented somewhere, please treat this as a documentation request. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Please document and support a reliable isolation contract for parallel headless `opencode run` workers. The current knobs are hard to reason about for orchestration: - `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` adds or overrides config lookup, but it does not isolate OpenCode's global data/state. - Running workers with separate generated `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` directories still allowed one worker to hit `database is locked`. - Synthetic probes with per-worker `OPENCODE_DB` did not produce a working parallel run. - Synthetic probes with per-worker `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and `XDG_STATE_HOME` avoided the obvious shared profile but did not complete a one-line `opencode run` sentinel in the bounded test window. A coordinator needs a documented way to launch independent workers without sharing enough local state to deadlock or produce SQLite lock failures. A simple contract could be something like: ```bash OPENCODE_HOME="$worker_root" opencode run ... ``` or a documented combination of environment variables that isolates: - database/session storage; - global lock state; - auth/provider config; - cache/log paths; - plugin and MCP side effects. If true process-level isolation is intentionally unsupported, it would still help to document that `opencode run` is single-writer per user profile and recommend a supported coordinator pattern for parallel agent workflows. The use case is repository audit/verification orchestration: a coordinator launches multiple top-level `opencode run` workers in parallel, each with its own prompt and output directory, and expects each worker to either complete or fail independently.
signal.author: coygeek

signal.title: Headless opencode run can hang after model banner under parallel startup
signal.text: ### Description In a parallel headless workflow, some `opencode run` processes can reach the model banner and then make no further progress. In my reproduction, this happened while a sibling worker failed with `database is locked`. The stuck worker logs contained only: ```text > build · cohere/north-mini-code:free ``` No tool calls, prompt reads, streamed model output, retry message, timeout, or error followed. The processes stayed alive until the coordinator terminated them externally. This may be another symptom of the same shared-state contention discussed in #21215 and #29395, but the user-visible failure mode is different: the worker does not crash, it just appears parked after model initialization. Expected behavior: if headless `opencode run` is waiting on database/state/provider initialization, it should surface that state and either complete, retry, or fail within a bounded window. ### Plugins `--pure` was used in synthetic probes. The wrapper run used a generated project-local config for an OpenAI-compatible OpenRouter provider. ### OpenCode version `1.17.8` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider/model. In my reproduction, the model was `openrouter/cohere/north-mini-code:free`. 2. Launch three headless workers close together: ```bash for worker in 1 2 3; do ( OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR="$generated_config_dir" \ opencode run \ --dangerously-skip-permissions \ -m openrouter/cohere/north-mini-code:free \ --title "worker-$worker" \ "Return a short sentinel." ) & done wait ``` 3. In the observed run: - one worker failed immediately with `database is locked`; - sibling workers printed only `> build · cohere/north-mini-code:free`; - those sibling workers did not emit further progress or a terminal error within the bounded test window. ### Screenshot and/or share link No screenshot/share link. The model banner excerpt is included above. ### Operating System macOS 26.5.1 ### Terminal Headless `opencode run` launched from tmux windows in zsh.
signal.author: coygeek

signal.title: Canva MCP: Tool registration fails with schema validation error "enum[0]: cannot be empty" despite successful authentication
signal.text: Canva MCP tools fail to load with schema validation error (enum[0]: cannot be empty) Environment OpenCode Version: 1.17.9 OS: Windows 11 Canva MCP: https://mcp.canva.com/mcp MCP Status: Connected and authenticated Models tested: Gemma 4 31B IT Gemini 2.5 Flash Result: Same error across models Description The Canva MCP server successfully connects and authenticates, but any attempt to use Canva tools causes tool registration to fail before execution. The error appears to occur while OpenCode/provider tooling is processing Canva MCP tool schemas. Reproduction Steps Configure Canva MCP: { "mcp": { "canva": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.canva.com/mcp" } } } Authenticate: opencode mcp auth canva Verify connection: opencode mcp list Output: ✓ canva connected https://mcp.canva.com/mcp Ask OpenCode: Create a Canva presentation about climate change with 5 slides. Actual Result GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[25].parameters.properties[operations].items.any_of[8].properties[formatting].properties[link].any_of[0].enum[0]: cannot be empty No Canva tool is executed. Expected Result Canva MCP tools should load successfully and the design should be created. Additional Information opencode mcp debug canva reports: Auth status: ✓ authenticated Access token: present Refresh token: present Connection successful (already authenticated) The issue persists after upgrading from OpenCode 1.15.13 to 1.17.9. Because authentication succeeds and the same schema error occurs across multiple models, this appears to be either: A Canva MCP tool schema incompatibility, or An OpenCode MCP schema translation/validation issue. The failing schema path appears to be: function_declarations[25] .parameters.properties[operations] .items.any_of[8] .properties[formatting] .properties[link] .any_of[0] .enum[0]

Opening the second directory reuses the window of the first one, so only one of them can ever be shown. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Clone the same remote into two separate local directories: - ~/path-a/myrepo (origin: git@<git-host>:<group>/myrepo.git) - ~/path-b/myrepo (origin: git@<git-host>:<group>/myrepo.git) 2. signal.title: fix(mcp): tool key collision when server or tool names contain underscores
signal.text: ### Description MCP tool keys are built as sanitize(server) + _ + sanitize(tool), but sanitize() preserves _ and -. This makes the _ separator ambiguous, so different (server, tool) pairs can produce identical keys and silently overwrite each other. For example, server foo tool bar_baz and server foo_bar tool baz both produce key foo_bar_baz. Notably, catalog.ts:103 already uses : as separator for prompts/resources (which sanitize rejects), but the tool registration path at index.ts:646 still uses _. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure two MCP servers named foo and foo_bar 2. Server foo exposes tool bar_baz, server foo_bar exposes tool baz 3. Only one tool appears in the tool list — the other is silently lost ### Suggested fix Use : as separator in packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts:646, matching the pattern already used for prompts/resources in catalog.ts:103. ### Operating System Windows 11

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Config schema should tolerate unknown fields instead of failing all session loading
signal.text: - [X] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request When the opencode config file (`opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc`) contains a root-level field that is not defined in the Config schema (e.g., `"files": {}`), opencode throws `ConfigInvalidError` and **refuses to load all sessions**. The Config JSON Schema uses `"additionalProperties": false` at the root level, so any unrecognized property causes a fatal validation error. This is overly fragile: a single misplaced key should produce a warning, not crash the entire application. **Suggested approach:** 1. Unknown properties should be logged as warnings and skipped (`warn-and-skip`) 2. Either relax `additionalProperties` at the root level, or explicitly ignore unrecognized fields during config parsing 3. If a config section is invalid, skip that section and continue with defaults for the rest 4. Show a non-blocking notification ("Unknown config field 'files' – ignoring") instead of crashing session loading

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Encourage structured Markdown authoring to improve agent-parsability
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Summary opencode's system prompts discourage the use of structured Markdown (headings, nested lists) in model outputs. That guidance was applied in the system prompts and has historically been framed as TUI-oriented style. However, the more important target for structured formatting is not ephemeral agent responses but the persistent Markdown artifacts authored and checked in. Those artifacts are stored verbatim and consumed by agents and other tooling. Flattening structure reduces machine-parsability, making it harder for agents and tooling to reliably extract sections, lists, and structured data. ## Why this matters - Structured Markdown provides stable, machine-friendly anchors that models and tooling can use to locate, extract, and re-use information; the heading tokens and indentation for nested lists are load-bearing. - Markdown artifacts authored inside opencode are durable, checked-in objects. Prompts that suppress structure therefore harm agent-to-agent and agent-to-program workflows that rely on parsable artifacts. - The explicit ban on nested lists and the instruction to avoid real headings were copied from upstream Codex CLI prompts and later minimized, removing the original rendering-vs-consumption rationale. ## Proposed change 1. Update system prompts to encourage structured Markdown when the content is intended as an artifact or for downstream processing. 2. Add a short comment in each prompt explaining the rendering-vs-consumption rationale, so future edits don't strip it during minimization. 3. Consider introducing a separate structured-output channel or a post-processing rendering pass that transforms structured model output for TUI display while preserving a machine-consumable canonical form.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: propagate outgoing trace context to spawned tool subprocesses
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem When OpenCode spawns tool subprocesses (shell tool, stdio MCP transports, LSP servers, formatter, git, etc.), it does not propagate the active OTel context. Tools that emit their own telemetry land in disconnected root traces, breaking continuity between the OpenCode invocation and the work the tool performed. ## Expected behavior When OpenCode spawns a tool subprocess, the OTel context active at spawn time should be propagated via the standard `TRACEPARENT` (and `TRACESTATE` when non-empty) env vars, per the [OTel environment variable carrier spec](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/context/api-propagators/#textmap-propagator). Tool subprocesses that emit OTel-instrumented telemetry should appear as children of opencode's invocation trace. ## Scope Every subprocess spawn site: - Shell tool (`packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts`) - Stdio MCP transports (`packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts` → `StdioClientTransport`) - All Effect-based `spawner.spawn` callers (LSP servers, git/worktree, format, snapshot, project, etc.) — these route through `packages/core/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts`, so a single injection point there covers them all. ## Related Sibling to #18801, which covers the inbound direction (extracting `traceparent` from incoming HTTP requests). Together they close the loop on trace context propagation across opencode's process boundaries

signal.title: Agents silently invoke premium-cost models without cost disclosure, can burn maintainer grants
signal.text: ## Summary The `task` tool allows agents to invoke `expert-reviewer` subagent which uses `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` — a premium Copilot-billed model. There is no cost disclosure before invocation, no user confirmation, and the agent can ignore explicit user instructions to use cheaper alternatives when trigger words appear in subsequent prompts. ## Impact on a real project A maintainer of `linuxboot/heads` (Copilot Maintainer Grant) lost their entire **1,500 monthly credits** in a single session: 1. First `expert-reviewer` call consumed **871 credits** (58% of monthly grant) 2. User explicitly instructed the agent to use `reviewer` instead 3. Agent reverted to `expert-reviewer` on every subsequent request containing the word "expert" 4. Final 3 calls returned **empty task results** — premium credits charged, zero output delivered 5. Total: ~10 calls, full monthly grant depleted ## Root cause The agent configuration at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` defines: - `reviewer` → `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` (free tier) - `expert-reviewer` → `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` (premium, Copilot-billed) There is no mechanism for: 1. **Cost metadata** — the `task` tool does not disclose that one subagent costs credits and another does not 2. **User confirmation** — no "this will cost X credits, continue?" prompt 3. **Instruction persistence** — once user says "use reviewer", the agent should not revert to premium on trigger words 4. **Resource limits** — no way to say "hard-block all premium-cost invocations" ## Suggested fix 1. Add `credit_cost` or `premium: true` metadata to agent/subagent definitions in `opencode.json`, surfaced in the system prompt 2. Require explicit user confirmation before any premium-cost subagent invocation 3. Honor explicit subagent restrictions from user instructions across the session 4. Provide a config-level "premium: never" flag **Reported by:** @tlaurion, maintainer linuxboot/heads **Evidence:** Full session transcript available showing the pattern

signal.title: Render process freezes/crashes when opening session with large diffs
signal.text: **Note: This bug is specific to the desktop/GUI version (Electron), not the terminal TUI version. The TUI does not have this issue.** ### Description When opening a session that contains a very large file diff (e.g., a 20KB+ patch with garbled encoding), the render process becomes unresponsive and may crash entirely. The root cause is the `execEditLength` function in the diff algorithm (`diffLines` → `structuredPatch` → `createTwoFilesPatch`), which has O(n²) complexity and hangs on large patches. This occurred 3 times on opencode v1.16.2 (Electron 41.2.1, Chrome 146) on Windows: 1. **Temporary freeze (4s)** — renderer unresponsive then recovered 2. **Long freeze (35s)** — 14 unresponsive samples collected, eventually recovered 3. **Crash (no recovery)** — Electron crash reporter triggered, minidump generated (33MB) Full stack trace from all 3 occurrences: ``` at execEditLength (main-EPcHbCKO.js:42291) at diffWithOptionsObj → diffLines → structuredPatch at createTwoFilesPatch → parseDiffFromFile at fileDiffFromContent → fileDiffFromPatch → resolveFileDiff ``` ### OpenCode version 1.16.2 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows ConHost (ConsoleWindowClass)

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Per-Provider Quota-Aware Auto-Retry with Configurable Reset Schedule
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Problem OpenCode's session retry already parses `retry-after` headers and recognises `FreeUsageLimitError` / `GoUsageLimitError` (see `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts`), but the handling is essentially hardcoded to the OpenCode Go subscription: - `GoUsageLimitError` already extracts `metadata.limitName` (`"5 hour" | "weekly" | "monthly"`) and `retry-after`, then surfaces it in the UI as *"X hour usage limit reached. It will reset in Y hours."* — but the session does **not** actually wait for that reset; it just retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff. - Providers **other than OpenCode Go** (e.g. users bringing their own keys to fixed-window-quota providers) hit a 429 with no `metadata.limitName` in the body. The retry logic falls back to exponential backoff, exhausts the 5 attempts, and gives up — exactly when the user is most likely to need an automatic wait-and-resume. In short: OpenCode already has the *display* half of quota handling (for Go) but not the *wait-until-reset* half, and the whole thing is only wired up for Go. ### Proposed solution 1. **Generalise the existing quota classification.** `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts` already has the primitives (`LimitName = "5 hour" | "weekly" | "monthly"`, `retry-after` parsing). Expose them through a per-provider config so any provider can declare its own reset schedule. 2. **Read the schedule from `provider.<id>.quota`, not `provider.options.quota`.** The `options` block is pass-through to the AI SDK (`timeout`, `chunkTimeout`, `setCacheKey`, `baseURL`, `apiKey`, `headers`); quota / retry are OpenCode-internal behaviour, so they belong next to `options` rather than inside it. 3. **Actually wait for the next reset** instead of giving up after 5 exponential attempts. **Config** (extends the existing `provider` block; field names follow the camelCase convention used by `baseURL`, `chunkTimeout`, `setCacheKey`): { "provider": { "<id>": { "options": { "...": "..." }, "quota": { "resetTimes": ["00:00", "05:00", "10:00", "15:00", "20:00"], "weeklyResetDay": "monday", "monthlyResetDay": 1 }, "retry": { "maxRetriesPerWindow": 5, "maxTotalRetries": 50 } } } } **Behaviour when a quota error is hit:** 1. Classify error → 5h / weekly / monthly / transient (reuse the existing `LimitName` types from `retry.ts`). 2. 5h hit → next reset from `resetTimes`, sleep, resume. 3. Weekly / monthly hit → surface a clear *"X limit reached, resets on …"* message; no auto-retry inside the session. 4. After `maxRetriesPerWindow` failures inside one window, queue for the next window. 5. Hard ceiling `maxTotalRetries` prevents runaway sessions. **Backwards compatibility:** providers without a `quota` block fall back to today's behaviour (exponential backoff, 5 attempts). ### Related issues - #43126 — auto pause/resume on known reset time (closest match — semantic of "wait for the right reset" already exists, but no per-provider schema) - #39790 / #39791 — fixed-window quota should not retry blindly - #32423 — provider-specific rate limiting (RPM throttle, orthogonal) - #37412 — `ProviderConfig.options.maxRetries/...` proposal (this extends that schema by adding `provider.quota` / `provider.retry` at the top level) - #21960 / #17648 / #30510 / #41848 — retry has no max attempt count

signal.title: feat(opencode): Message logger
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #29186 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds configurable LLM request/response logging via `experimental.log_messages` (`"info"`, `"debug"`, `"trace"`) and wires it into both the native and AI SDK runtimes. - `"info"` — logs messages + response text (Effect info level) - `"debug"` — adds generation params (Effect debug level) - `"trace"` — adds the raw provider-native request body (native runtime only) at Effect trace level; requires `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` or `TRACE` to be visible Responses are coalesced: one `LLM response` entry per provider turn (emitted when the terminal event passes), not one per streamed delta — on both runtimes. Requests are logged once per call in both runtimes. Notes: - The AI SDK runtime never sees the provider-native wire body (the AI SDK builds it internally), so on that path `"trace"` carries the same payload as `"debug"`. - Logs can contain full transcripts (prompts, tool I/O) — the config option now says to treat log destinations as sensitive. - Adds `TRACE` as a valid `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL` value (needed for the trace tier to be reachable; the runtime's minimum level previously capped at `DEBUG`). signal.title: v1.18.21 repeatedly continues complete responses with finish=unknown
signal.text: ### Description OpenCode 1.18.21 can repeatedly continue a complete assistant response when the provider labels it `finish=unknown`. With `opencode/x-preview-f-free`, the provider sometimes returns complete, usable text while reporting `unknown` and zero token usage. Since #43892 makes the prompt loop continue after every `unknown` finish, OpenCode submits another turn. If subsequent completed responses also end with `unknown`, the loop continues without a bound. Sanitized event sequence from one run: ```text step_finish reason=unknown output_tokens=0 # five empty attempts text bytes=44879 # complete, syntactically valid requested JSON step_finish reason=unknown output_tokens=0 text bytes=50319 # redundant continuation step_finish reason=unknown output_tokens=0 step_start # another continuation begins ``` The process remained active after the first complete response and had to be terminated. This can duplicate or corrupt output, hang unattended runs, and consume unbounded provider requests. The empty-response case in #41469 and #43856 should be retried. This report concerns the distinct output-bearing case. The test added in #43895 covers `unknown -> continuation -> stop`; it does not cover a provider that returns complete text and continues to label the finish `unknown`. Expected behavior: recovery from `unknown` must be bounded. An empty `unknown` may be retried, but a substantive output-bearing `unknown` must not cause unlimited automatic continuations. ### Plugins None. ### OpenCode version 1.18.21 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a long, non-interactive request against a provider that can return usable output with an `unknown` finish, for example: `opencode run --format json --model opencode/x-preview-f-free --variant high "Return one moderately long, self-contained JSON object as your entire response."` 2. Inspect the JSON event stream. 3. When a complete text event is followed by `step_finish reason=unknown`, observe that OpenCode starts another model turn instead of completing the command. 4. If the provider labels the next response `unknown` as well, observe another continuation. The provider behavior is intermittent. The event sequence above is from a captured occurrence. ### Screenshot and/or share link The sanitized event sequence is included above. The original response content is unrelated to the transport failure and cannot be shared. ### Operating System Windows 11 with Ubuntu 22.04.5 under WSL2 (kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2) ### Terminal Non-interactive WSL2 shell invoking the OpenCode Windows CLI (`opencode.exe`)

Origin-rooted paths resolve from the origin, path-relative values resolve beneath the configured server base, absolute HTTP(S) URLs remain unchanged, and malformed or non-HTTP(S) values enter each implementation's existing typed error channel. ## How - `packages/opencode/src/account/account.ts` resolves the verification URL inside `Account.login` and maps invalid values to `AccountServiceError`. - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts` resolves the verification URL inside the existing V2 OAuth method and maps invalid values through `Integration.AuthorizationError`. - Adds production-shaped and malformed-response regressions to each implementation's existing test suite. ## Scope This does not change account APIs, integration APIs, endpoints, credentials, token polling, or the Console response. It only replaces string concatenation at the two verification URL boundaries on `dev`. ## Testing - `bun run test test/account/service.test.ts` from `packages/opencode`: 15 passed - `bun run test test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 12 passed - `bun typecheck` from `packages/opencode` - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core` - Push hook: repository-wide Turbo typecheck, 30 tasks passed - `git diff --check` ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client as Account/Core client participant Console as Console API participant Browser Client->>Console: POST /console/auth/device/code Console-->>Client: verification_uri_complete=/console/device?... Client-->>Client: Resolve against server URL Client->>Browser: Open https://opencode.ai/console/device?... ``` Ports the fix from #44021 to `dev`.
